clue.text: Would reportedly stick with impasse

parts.note: 'would' said out loud is identical to 'wood', and a log is a piece of wood
to stick or jam is to become stuck fast

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a deadlock says they'd like to stick with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' tells you 'Would' is to be taken by its sound, WOOD, which then gives a synonym, LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A logjam is a deadlock where nothing can move, which is exactly an impasse.

clue.text: Camilla, not in the morning, replanted tree

indicators.note: replanted fits the tree surface while signalling the letters set in new places
says the morning letters are taken out

parts.note: AM means before noon

explanation.surface: Camilla replants a tree in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes AM from CAMILLA, leaving CILLA, which 'replanted' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The lilac is a flowering shrub or small tree.

clue.text: Preserve bachelor, with the Parisian female at end of day, put on a spicy dish

indicators.note: in a down entry, the earlier pieces sit on top of the next one

parts.note: jam is a fruit preserve
French 'à la' means 'at the', with the feminine article

indicators.note: takes the last letter of day

explanation.surface: Instructions for a meal: jam, a bachelor and a French woman before a spicy dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'à la' is French for 'at the' (feminine), giving ALA.
explanation.definitionFit: Jambalaya is a Cajun rice dish with spicy sausage, chicken or seafood.

clue.text: Make-up mother used to cover a blemish

indicators.note: says the mother word wraps around the rest

parts.note: MA is a familiar word for mother
a scar is a mark or blemish

explanation.surface: Mother applies make-up to hide a blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is cosmetic colouring for eyelashes, a kind of make-up.

clue.text: False profession

parts.note: a profession here is a declaration or claim, not a job; a false claim is a sham

explanation.surface: Reads like a remark about a bogus career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'profession' looks like an occupation, but it means 'professing', claiming something.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretence is a show or claim that is not genuine, a false declaration.

clue.text: Writer uses it to make a point

definitions.text: Writer uses it to make a point

parts.words: Writer uses it to make a point
parts.note: 'make a point' sounds like arguing, but here it means sharpening a pencil tip

explanation.surface: Sounds like a rhetorical device an author uses to argue.
explanation.definitionFit: This device puts a sharp tip on a pencil, so someone writing uses it for a literal point.

clue.text: Person who's out before their time

definitions.text: Person who's out before their time

parts.words: Person who's out before their time
parts.note: suggests someone ahead of their era, but means a prisoner who gets out before the sentence ends

explanation.surface: Sounds like a visionary ahead of their age.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who breaks out of jail is free before their sentence has been served.

clue.text: Wrongly warn Henry about large sea-creature

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters of warn are out of order

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Someone gives Henry a mistaken warning about a big sea animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The narwhal is an Arctic whale with a long spiral tusk.

clue.text: Denounced executive officer who was highly thought of

parts.note: an exec is an executive
rated means highly regarded

explanation.surface: A well-regarded company officer is publicly condemned.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to curse or condemn, so denounced fits.

clue.text: Beat graduates one day in August

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or beat
MAs are Masters of Arts, graduates

explanation.surface: Graduates beat someone on a day in August.
explanation.walkthrough: LAMMAS Day, 1 August, is an old English harvest festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Lammas is the traditional harvest festival held on the first of August.

clue.text: Tune Ron composed about to be included in dreamy piano piece

indicators.note: says the next piece goes inside the jumbled letters
composed suggests the letters of the words being set out afresh, as music is

parts.note: C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A man named Ron writes a tune for a dreamy piano piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' looks like part of the musical story but is the anagram signal; C for 'about' (circa) is set inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturne is a short, reflective piano composition evoking night, as made famous by Chopin.

clue.text: State one put most of biscuit on seafood

parts.note: CAL is short for California
A is the indefinite article, one

indicators.note: says the word for biscuit loses its last letter

parts.note: a Marie is a plain sweet biscuit

explanation.surface: Someone puts a broken biscuit on top of their seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: A Marie is a plain round biscuit popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamari is squid prepared as food, a seafood dish.

clue.text: Drug dealer held by copper and doorkeeper

parts.note: P stands for a penny, a copper coin
an usher shows people in at a door

explanation.surface: A drug dealer is caught by a policeman and a doorman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the coin, a penny, P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pusher is slang for someone who sells illegal narcotics.

clue.text: No way sad performing in these times

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters acting out a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A performer insists they are not sad these days.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowadays is an adverb meaning at the present time.

clue.text: Not a rare amount becoming higher figure

indicators.note: says the article a is excluded from the pool
becoming signals the remaining letters turning into something new

explanation.surface: A sum that is not rare grows into a bigger number.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A from RARE AMOUNT and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: In a fraction the numerator is the number written above the line, the upper figure.

clue.text: Bird with broken leg to take food outside

indicators.note: says the eating word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to eat is to take food

indicators.note: broken means the letters of leg are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird with an injured leg must still eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' reads as an injury but signals the anagram; 'outside' tells you which piece wraps the other.
explanation.definitionFit: An eaglet is a young eagle, a bird.

clue.text: Trying porridge with fish

parts.note: gruel is thin porridge
the ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Porridge with fish is a hard meal to face.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruelling means exhausting and demanding, so trying.

clue.text: Pattern of the law

definitions.meaning: a design of small pieces forming a picture
relating to Moses, the law-giver, as in the law of Moses

explanation.surface: Sounds like a legal precedent.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosaic is a pattern of tiles; Mosaic also means relating to Moses, whose law is the Mosaic law.

clue.text: Orange pottery

explanation.surface: An orange-glazed pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a kind of mandarin orange; Satsuma ware is Japanese earthenware.

clue.text: One who could have plenty of time and might become 5

definitions.text: One who could have plenty of time and might become 5

parts.words: One who could have plenty of time and might become 5
parts.note: 'time' is a prison sentence, and 5 refers to the jailbreaker of 5 Down

explanation.surface: Sounds like a person of leisure.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner serves a long sentence and may break out to become an escaper.

clue.text: Weapon belonging to you and me Edward covered

parts.note: an arm is a weapon
our means belonging to us
ED is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Edward reveals a weapon he shares with us.
explanation.definitionFit: Armoured means protected by a hard covering, so covered.

clue.text: Middle Eastern gun on this bomb

parts.note: ME is short for Middle East
a gat is slang for a pistol

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern weapon is mounted on a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A megaton bomb has explosive power equal to a million tons of TNT.

clue.text: It is to be distributed during speech after first ring has been removed

indicators.text: after first ring has been removed
indicators.note: a ring is round like the letter O, here the initial letter, taken away

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Something handed out during a speech after a bell has been silenced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' is the circle shape O, the first letter of ORATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A ration is a fixed allowance that is shared out to people.

clue.text: Boxer dog is being held by independent lieutenant

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog

indicators.note: says the word is goes inside the following letters

explanation.surface: A boxer dog kept by an independent army officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' looks like the dog breed but is a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pugilist is a person who fights with fists, a boxer.

clue.text: John does not have one indication of vacancy

indicators.note: says the next piece is missing

parts.note: john is slang for a lavatory
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: John lacks a sign of somewhere vacant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man's name; it is slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A 'to let' sign shows a property is available to rent.

clue.text: Moving in, turn on one of a pair of pivots

definitions.text: one of a pair of pivots

indicators.note: moving suggests the letters shifting into new places

explanation.surface: Instructions for a machine: move in, switch on, find the pivot.
explanation.definitionFit: A trunnion is either of two projecting pins on which a cannon or similar object pivots.

clue.text: Speak endlessly about joint type of warfare

indicators.note: says the shortened word goes around the next piece
says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to talk is to speak
a rib is a joint of meat

explanation.surface: Someone talks on and on about a joint of meat or of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' is a cut of meat here, a rib; 'endlessly' drops the last letter and 'about' makes the shortened word go round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal warfare is fighting between clans or ethnic groups.

clue.text: Car delayed first during very hot day

indicators.note: says one piece goes inside the hot-day word

parts.note: a roaster is a sweltering day

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of delayed

explanation.surface: A car held up on a scorching day.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadster is an open two-seater sports car.

clue.text: One of shooting-party back to receive some precious metal

indicators.note: says the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a gun is a member of a shooting party
to get is to receive

explanation.surface: A shooter steps back to collect a gold find.
